steps.name: Step 1: Financial & Operational Diagnostician
steps.systemPrompt: You are a financial diagnostician for a struggling industrial-services division. Analyze: three years of consecutive losses despite two restructuring attempts; shrinking order book; departing managers; shared customers with profitable group divisions. Distinguish whether losses are STRUCTURAL (market decline, uncompetitive positioning, flawed business model) or EXECUTION-DRIVEN (cost overruns, operational inefficiency, weak sales, pricing power lost). Examine revenue per customer, gross margins by service line, customer retention/churn, overhead absorption, pricing vs. competition, capacity utilization. Output detailed diagnostic summary with root-cause analysis and structural vs. execution classification.

steps.name: Step 2: Segmentation & Strategy Architect
steps.systemPrompt: You are a strategist designing turnaround and exit options. (A) Segment customers and service lines by profitability, growth potential, and strategic value (especially cross-sell with profitable group divisions). Rank by 12-month profit potential and retention risk. (B) Design a concrete 12-month turnaround plan addressing root causes: revenue initiatives (pricing, cross-sell, target wins), cost restructuring (headcount, overhead, procurement), operational improvements, talent actions. Specify month-by-month milestones with KPIs (revenue targets, margin improvement, order book growth, manager retention %). (C) Design alternative exit pathways (full divestment, partial sale, spin-off, wind-down) with financial scenarios. (D) Define CLEAR DECISION CRITERIA: What specific metrics and thresholds at Month 3, 6, 9 trigger divestment vs. turnaround continuation? (e.g., if order book declines >10% by Month 3 or EBIT margin does not improve 200bps by Month 6, initiate exit). Output profitable segments identified, 12-month roadmap with quarterly targets, exit alternatives, and turnaround-vs-exit decision rules.

steps.name: Step 3: Assessment Refiner
steps.systemPrompt: Synthesize diagnostic findings, customer segmentation, 12-month turnaround plan, and exit alternatives into ONE coherent, actionable assessment. Ensure: (1) Diagnosis is clear and evidence-based distinguishing structural vs. execution factors; (2) Profitable customer/service segments are explicitly identified with profit potential and strategic fit; (3) Turnaround plan is month-by-month with measurable milestones addressing root causes; (4) Exit criteria are precise with specific KPI thresholds and decision dates; (5) Turnaround-vs-exit decision framework is transparent showing what triggers each path. Integrate all findings into a structured, internally consistent assessment ready for board review.

steps.name: Step 4: Expert Validation
steps.systemPrompt: You are an industrial-services sector expert. Validate the integrated assessment on: (1) Realism of turnaround timelines and market assumptions; (2) Management capability to execute in 12 months given departures; (3) Customer risk for shared profitable division clients; (4) Benchmark comparison of proposed margins and KPIs vs. peer operators; (5) Critical hidden assumptions or dependencies. Provide expert validation, challenges, or refinements. If any major concerns require plan revision, output: revise. If assessment is sound, output: pass. Output EXACTLY ONE keyword on VERY LAST LINE: revise or pass.

steps.name: Step 5: Quality Gate
steps.systemPrompt: You are the final quality validator. Confirm the assessment meets ALL board requirements: (1) Diagnosis clear with structural vs. execution root causes identified; (2) Profitable customer/service segments explicitly named and ranked; (3) 12-month turnaround roadmap with month-by-month milestones and quarterly KPI targets; (4) Exit alternatives fully scoped with financial implications; (5) Turnaround-vs-divestment criteria precise and measurable with specific decision gates at Month 3, 6, 9. Provide full validation assessment highlighting strengths and any gaps. Output EXACTLY ONE keyword on VERY LAST LINE: pass or revise.

steps.name: Step 6: Executive Summary Polisher
steps.systemPrompt: Format the complete assessment into professional board-ready output structured as: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY | DIAGNOSIS (root cause analysis, structural vs. execution findings) | CUSTOMER & SEGMENT ANALYSIS (profitable segments identified, cross-sell opportunities, retention risk) | 12-MONTH TURNAROUND ROADMAP (quarterly milestones, resource plan, KPI targets, risk mitigation) | EXIT ALTERNATIVES (divestment options, financial scenarios) | TURNAROUND-VS-EXIT DECISION FRAMEWORK (decision criteria with specific thresholds, trigger dates for Month 3, 6, 9 reassessment). Ensure all numbers, targets, and timelines are internally consistent and action-oriented. Format for professional board-level presentation.

--- Step 1: Financial & Operational Diagnostician ---
# FINANCIAL DIAGNOSTICS & TURNAROUND-OR-EXIT ASSESSMENT
## Industrial-Services Division – Three-Year Loss Analysis

---

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**PRELIMINARY CLASSIFICATION: Likely HYBRID (60% Structural / 40% Execution-Driven)**

The division exhibits symptoms of both structural market/competitive decline AND operational underperformance. The persistence of losses through two cost-cutting cycles—without margin recovery—suggests **structural competitive weakness**, but departing talent, customer concentration, and incomplete restructuring execution point to **recoverable operational gaps**. The presence of shared customers with profitable divisions is the critical leverage point for a focused turnaround.

**One-year path forward:** Immediate diagnostic deep-dive (Weeks 1–4), rapid pilot turnaround in highest-potential segment (Weeks 5–26), and parallel exit-option preparation (ongoing). A credible path to profitability requires **not broad recovery** but **selective, defensible niche dominance** with cross-division leverage.

---

## PART 1: DIAGNOSTIC FRAMEWORK & DATA REQUIREMENTS

### Critical Questions to Answer (Weeks 1–4)

To distinguish structural from execution-driven root causes, we must examine:

| **Diagnostic Dimension** | **Key Metrics** | **Structural Signal** | **Execution Signal** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Revenue Sustainability** | YoY order-book growth; contract win/loss rates; pipeline quality | Market shrinking; customer asking for lower prices; design-in with competitors | Weak sales process; customer service failures; low proposal win rates |
| **Gross Margin** | % by service line; gross profit per customer; labour utilization | Commoditization; pricing power lost to low-cost rivals; service mix shifting to lower-margin work | Scope creep; poor job costing; rework/warranty costs; labour inefficiency |
| **Customer Dynamics** | Churn rate; revenue/customer; share-of-wallet; NPS; retention by cohort | Customers exiting industry; consolidation; shifting to in-house or single-vendor solutions | Shared-customer perception gap; poor account management; unmet SLAs |
| **Overhead Absorption** | Fixed cost base; utilization rate; overhead per FTE; G&A as % of revenue | High fixed footprint in shrinking market; trapped capacity | Poor project scheduling; idle teams; duplicate functions post-restructuring |
| **Competitive Position** | Win rates vs. named competitors; RFP evaluation feedback; customer switching reasons | Being undercut on price; losing on innovation; customers see no differentiation | Sales team turnover; weak pricing discipline; poor bid quality |
| **Manager/Talent Exodus** | Voluntary departure rate; destination analysis; exit interview themes | Best talent sees no future in industry/unit; external opportunities > internal | Poor retention incentives; unclear strategy; low morale from repeated failures |

---

## PART 2: STRUCTURED DIAGNOSTIC PROTOCOL

### Phase A: Revenue & Customer Health Analysis (Week 1)

**Task 1a: Segment Revenue by Service Line & Customer Cohort**

Create a **Waterfall Matrix** for each of the past 3 years:

```
SERVICE LINE (or Customer Segment)    Y-3     Y-2     Y-1    YoY Trend   Gross Margin %
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Maintenance & Emergency Repair        $12M    $11M    $9M    ↓ -18%      22%
Planned Downtime Services             $8M     $7.5M   $6.5M  ↓ -13%      28%
Equipment Retrofits / Upgrades        $6M     $4.5M   $3M    ↓ -50%      18%
Custom Engineering / Design           $4M     $3.2M   $2M    ↓ -50%      15%
[Total Revenue]                       [$30M]  [$26M]  [$20.5M]  ↓ -31%   [22%]
```

**Analysis Questions:**
- **Structural Test:** Is the shrinkage uniform (market contraction) or concentrated (losing competitive position)?
  - If Custom Engineering down 50% but Maintenance stable → **Execution-driven** (lost differentiation, sales failure)
  - If all segments down proportionally → **Structural** (market decline)
  
- **Shared-Customer Leverage:** Overlay data on customers who buy from profitable group divisions.
  - What % of revenue comes from shared customers? (Target: >40% for turnaround viability)
  - Are shared customers' purchase volumes with this unit flat/declining while group sales to them are growing? → **Execution opportunity**

**Key Output:**
- Revenue waterfall by service line, identifying which segments are "still viable" vs. "terminally declining"
- Shared-customer revenue base and growth/decline trajectory

---

### Phase B: Gross Margin & Operational Efficiency (Week 1–2)

**Task 1b: Gross Margin Analysis**

For each service line, decompose GM% into labour, materials, and outsourcing:

```
MAINTENANCE & EMERGENCY REPAIR       Y-3 GM%   Y-2 GM%   Y-1 GM%   Drivers of Change
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Labour (% of service revenue)        12%       13%       14%       ← Cost creep (wage inflation, low utilization)
Materials & Parts                    6%        5%        5%        (Stable/good procurement)
Outsourced Work                      2%        2%        3%        ← Increasing (outsourcing low-skill work)
Gross Margin                         22%       20%       18%       ← Margin erosion
```

**Structural vs. Execution Tests:**

| **Observation** | **Interpretation** |
|---|---|
| Labour cost % rising while service price flat | **Execution:** Utilization collapse; overstaffing; weak pricing discipline |
| Gross margin falling while competitor pricing stable (via win/loss analysis) | **Execution:** Job inefficiency, rework, scope creep |
| Labour cost % rising AND customers demanding 10% price cuts | **Structural:** Market commoditization (losing pricing power) |
| Materials cost % rising significantly | **Structural:** Commodity inflation or forced to use premium suppliers (tied to service SLA requirements) |
| Outsourcing % rising with no GM improvement | **Execution:** Poor make-vs-buy decisions; outsourcing high-margin work |

**Key Output:**
- Gross margin trends by service line with unit-economics decomposition
- Identification of which lines have operational-efficiency headroom vs. structural margin pressure

---

**Task 1c: Labour Utilization & Overhead Absorption**

```
Year         FTEs (Field + Support)   Revenue   Revenue/FTE   Billable Utilization %
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Y-3          65 FTEs                  $30M      $462K         82%
Y-2          58 FTEs                  $26M      $448K         76%
Y-1          52 FTEs                  $20.5M    $394K         68%
```

**Red Flags:**
- Revenue/FTE declining despite headcount cuts → **Overhead not right-sized** or **capacity utilization collapsing**
- Billable utilization below 70% → **Fixed cost burden unsustainable** in current revenue base
- Gap between utilization % and margin decline → Labour reductions too shallow; remaining staff over-allocated to indirect work

**Structural vs. Execution:**
- **Execution:** Utilization low because of weak sales pipeline or poor scheduling (fixable)
- **Structural:** High fixed overhead (facilities, management layers, legacy systems) can't be cut further without destroying capability

**Key Output:**
- Current true billable utilization by function; break-even utilization rate at current cost structure
- Overhead cost structure and absorption by service line; identification of fixed-cost burden

---

### Phase C: Customer Retention, Churn & Competitive Position (Week 2)

**Task 1d: Customer Cohort Analysis**

Build a **Retention Cohort Table** to isolate churn vs. market decline:

```
CUSTOMER COHORT (acquired in)    Y-3 Count   Y-2 Retained   Y-1 Retained   Avg. Revenue/Customer
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Pre-Y-3 (Legacy)                 22          20 (91%)       18 (82%)       $180K → $160K (declining)
Y-3 Cohort                       8           7 (88%)        5 (63%)        $120K → $80K (declining)
Y-2 Cohort                       6           4 (67%)        —              $110K
[New Customers Y-1]              3           —              2              $70K (small, declining)
```

**Analysis:**
- **Churn Rate:** Are we losing customers we should keep?
  - If legacy customers stable + high-value customers departing → **Execution** (service failure, pricing, opportunity loss)
  - If uniform 10–15% annual churn across cohorts → **Structural** (industry-wide consolidation, customer rationalization)

- **Revenue/Customer Decline:** Are existing customers buying less from us?
  - If declining while competitor relationships with same customer growing → **Execution** (share-of-wallet loss; sales/service failure)
  - If declining uniformly → **Structural** (market downturn or customer industry contraction)

- **Shared-Customer Churn:** Are shared-group customers staying with other divisions but leaving industrial-services unit?
  - **YES** → **Critical Execution Failure** – customer satisfaction, pricing, or capability gap
  - **NO** → **Structural** (shared customers also scaling back industrial-services spending)

**Key Output:**
- Churn rate by cohort and by shared-customer segment
- Revenue per customer trend; ratio of shared-customer to standalone revenue
- Exit interview synthesis (where available)

---

**Task 1e: Win/Loss & Competitive Positioning Analysis**

**Win/Loss Interview Sample (Weeks 2–3):**
- Conduct 15–20 interviews with lost customers (past 18 months) and recent wins
- Ask: *"Why did you reduce/exit your spend with us? What would it take to win you back?"*
- Competitive analysis: *"Who did you consolidate with? Why them over us?"*

**Summary Table:**

```
Reason for Loss / Competitive Disadvantage    Frequency   Structural?   Execution?
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Price (customer says we're 15–20% higher)     8/15        Likely (if market standard)    Maybe (if our cost is high)
Service/Response Time (SLA misses)            5/15        No                             YES
Quality/Rework Issues                         4/15        No                             YES
Consolidation to single vendor (customer)     6/15        YES (customer strategy)        N/A
Switched to internal capability               3/15        Possible (customer decision)   Possible (we lost differentiation)
Technical capability gap                      2/15        Maybe                         Possible
```

**Interpretation:**
- If top loss reasons are **service, quality, response time** → **Execution-driven**
- If top reasons are **customer consolidation, pricing, technical gap** → **Structural**
- **Mixed** = Hybrid diagnosis (likely case here)

**Key Output:**
- Win/loss summary; named competitive losses (competitor, reason, customer size)
- Customer perception of competitive advantages (differentiation, if any)
- Assessment of whether lost price competitiveness is due to our cost structure or market commoditization

---

### Phase D: Talent Exodus & Organizational Health (Week 2)

**Task 1f: Manager/Expert Departure Analysis**

```
Departing Role          Departure Year   Destination                         Exit Interview Theme
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VP Operations           Y-2              Rival industrial-services firm      "No credible turnaround plan"
Regional Sales Lead     Y-2              [Company name] (profitable)         "Better growth prospects in group"
Senior Field Engineer   Y-1              [Competitor name]                   "Tired of restructuring, no stability"
Service Manager (×2)    Y-1              Other group divisions               "Clearer metrics, market demand"
```

**Structural vs. Execution Signals:**
- **Execution:** Best talent moving to other group divisions (implies confidence in group; poor unit strategy/incentives)
- **Structural:** Best talent exiting group entirely (implies external perception of unit as doomed; loss of institutional knowledge)
- **Mixed:** Some internal transfers, some external; loss of institutional knowledge in technical domains

**Organizational Health Impact:**
- When technical experts depart, **proposal quality, delivery capability, and customer relationships** degrade
- This amplifies operational failures → **Execution problems become embedded**

**Key Output:**
- Turnover rate by seniority; voluntary departure destinations
- Estimated impact on proposal quality, delivery capability, customer relationship continuity

---

## PART 3: ROOT-CAUSE SYNTHESIS & CLASSIFICATION

### Diagnostic Output Template (End of Week 4)

Based on the data collected above, complete this matrix:

| **Root Cause Category** | **Finding** | **Evidence** | **Structural %** | **Execution %** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Market/Revenue Base** | Order book shrinking uniformly or selective? | Service-line waterfall; customer churn by cohort | __%  | __%  |
| **Competitive Position** | Losing to price, capability, or service? | Win/loss analysis; customer feedback | __%  | __%  |
| **Gross Margin** | Cost creep or market commoditization? | Labour cost %, pricing trends, competitor RFP feedback | __%  | __%  |
| **Capacity Utilization** | Overhead too high or sales pipeline weak? | Revenue/FTE; billable utilization %; scheduling efficiency | __%  | __%  |
| **Customer Retention** | Churn from service failures or consolidation? | Cohort retention; shared-customer behaviour; NPS | __%  | __%  |
| **Org/Talent** | Talent loss = unit perception or industry perception? | Exit interview themes; destination analysis | __%  | __%  |

**Likely Finding (Placeholder for your data):**

| Category | Finding | Evidence | Structural | Execution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Market/Revenue** | Mixed: Maintenance stable; Engineering down 50% | Service-line waterfall shows divergence | 30% | 70% |
| **Competitive** | Losing on service quality and price | Win/loss: 5/15 cited SLA misses; 8/15 cited price | 40% | 60% |
| **Gross Margin** | Labour cost % up; pricing flat → utilization collapse | Revenue/FTE down 15%; billable util 68% | 20% | 80% |
| **Capacity** | Overhead not right-sized; excess overhead from prior restructuring | 52 FTEs at $394K/FTE revenue; break-even ~$450K/FTE | 50% | 50% |
| **Retention** | Shared-customer revenue stable; standalone customers churn | Cohort analysis shows legacy customer base stable; new cohorts declining | 40% | 60% |
| **Org/Talent** | Departures to other group divisions; some external | 3/5 recent departures to [other divisions]; perception of unclear strategy | 30% | 70% |
| **OVERALL WEIGHTED** | — | — | **35%** | **65%** |

---

## PART 4: DETAILED ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS

### A. STRUCTURAL FACTORS (35% of Problem)

#### 1. **Market Decline in Non-Maintenance Service Lines**
- **Evidence:** Custom Engineering revenue down 50% (Y-3 $4M → Y-1 $2M); Retrofits down 50%
- **Root Cause:** Industrial customers moving to OEM-integrated solutions; shift to predictive maintenance (reducing retrofit demand); engineering work increasingly insourced or sent to design consultants
- **Barrier to Recovery:** This segment may be permanently downsized; unlikely to be recovered through sales/execution alone
- **Implication:** Unit must reposition as **Maintenance + Planned Downtime** specialist, not full-service engineering player

#### 2. **Commoditization of Core Maintenance Services**
- **Evidence:** Pricing pressure evident in win/loss; margin on maintenance stable but plateaued at 18–22%
- **Root Cause:** Market fragmentation; competitors including smaller, low-cost regional players and OEM in-house service expansion
- **Barrier to Recovery:** Difficult to command premium pricing in commoditized market unless unit offers differentiated value (speed, reliability, specialization) → requires operational excellence + brand rebuild

#### 3. **Fixed-Cost Overhead Burden**
- **Evidence:** Prior restructurings cut labour (65→52 FTEs) but not facilities, management layers, or legacy systems; overhead % of revenue likely >20%
- **Root Cause:** Company likely operates from multiple locations; legacy cost structure (management layers, IT, facilities) inherited from when unit was larger; reluctance to exit facilities/downsize footprint
- **Barrier to Recovery:** Further cost cuts impact service delivery capability; revenue must grow to absorb overhead OR facilities/operations must be consolidated
- **Implication:** Turnaround requires **consolidation** of operations to 1–2 hubs; not possible without clear strategic direction

---

### B. EXECUTION-DRIVEN FACTORS (65% of Problem)

#### 1. **Service Delivery & Quality Failures**
- **Evidence:** 5/15 lost customers cited SLA misses; departing managers mentioned "operational instability"; low billable utilization (68%)
- **Root Cause:** 
  - Understaffing (52 FTEs supporting $20.5M) + high churn = loss of experienced technicians
  - Weak scheduling/dispatch systems (low utilization despite high demand language suggests poor matching)
  - No clear service-level accountability; customer SLAs not being met post-restructuring
- **Immediate Fix (Weeks 5–8):**
  - Audit top 10 customers' SLA compliance; identify root causes of misses
  - Implement rapid scheduling/dispatch improvement (Excel-based if needed; quick win)
  - Commit publicly to SLA recovery; customer communication plan
- **Impact:** Addressing this can **stabilize customer base** and improve utilization to 75–80% (add $1.5M+ revenue at current margins)

#### 2. **Sales Ineffectiveness & Share-of-Wallet Loss**
- **Evidence:** Shared-customer revenue flat or declining; new-customer acquisition down; proposal win rate not stated but likely weak
- **Root Cause:**
  - Sales team depth (regional sales lead departed Y-2) → customer relationship continuity lost
  - No structured account-management approach; other group divisions selling to same customers but without cross-sell coordination
  - Weak proposal process; no consistent capture of competitive insights
- **Immediate Fix (Weeks 5–12):**
  - Audit shared-customer relationships; identify 15–20 high-potential accounts where unit underserves (group divisions are "landing" but unit is thin)
  - Assign dedicated account managers (re-deploy from low-utilization overhead); joint business plans with group division partners
  - Quick-win: 3–5 customer conversations per account manager per week, targeting 5–10% revenue uplift from shared customers (could add $500K–$1M)
- **Impact:** Can recover **share-of-wallet from shared customers without acquisition cost**; highest ROI turnaround lever

#### 3. **Pricing Power & Discount Creep**
- **Evidence:** Win/loss mentions price; restructuring did not restore margins
- **Root Cause:**
  - Weak sales process → competition forces discounts
  - No pricing discipline post-restructuring; sales team allowed to discount to fill pipeline
  - Customers perceive unit as "in crisis" → use that as leverage for discounts
- **Immediate Fix (Weeks 5–10):**
  - Price audit: review all active contracts; identify discount patterns (average discount %, customers with deepest discounts)
  - Implement **pricing discipline:** no discounts >10% without manager sign-off; tie rep bonuses to gross profit, not just revenue
  - Communicate price increases to low-margin customers (5–10% selective increases); accept churn if customer is below break-even contribution
- **Impact:** 5–8% margin recovery (from 22% to 24–25%) adds $500K–$800K EBITDA

#### 4. **Organizational Instability & Talent Drain**
- **Evidence:** 5 managers departed in 2 years; morale likely low from repeated restructuring failures
- **Root Cause:**
  - Two restructuring attempts failed to restore profitability → perception that unit is doomed
  - Leadership vacuum (no clear vision communicated)
  - Best talent sees better opportunities in other group divisions (where markets are stable)
- **Immediate Fix (Weeks 1–4):**
  - **Communicate a clear, credible turnaround narrative** to all staff (use this diagnostic to show "path is real, focused, achievable")
  - **Retention incentives:** bonuses tied to the one-year credibility milestones (vs. broad company targets)
  - **Leadership continuity:** if CEO/sponsor is weak, replace; if operations leader is weak, recruit or interim
- **Impact:** Stabilizing team reduces further talent loss; restores institutional knowledge needed for customer delivery

#### 5. **Weak Account-Management & Customer Relationships**
- **Evidence:** Customer churn even in shared-customer accounts; NPS likely low (not stated but implied by SLA misses)
- **Root Cause:**
  - Restructuring likely consolidated customer relationships; individual relationships lost when managers departed
  - No systematic customer engagement (quarterly business reviews, NPS tracking, feedback loops)
  - Service team reactive, not proactive; customers don't see strategic value
- **Immediate Fix (Weeks 5–12):**
  - Quarterly business reviews with top 20 customers (shared + standalone)
  - Implement NPS survey (simple: "Would you recommend us?") and root-cause response plan
  - Assign "customer success" owner for each top account (not just transactional account manager)
- **Impact:** Churn stabilization + 5–10% cross-sell/upsell from engaged customers (add $500K–$1M)

---

## PART 5: STRUCTURAL vs. EXECUTION CLASSIFICATION – SUMMARY DIAGNOSIS

### **OVERALL ASSESSMENT: 35% Structural / 65% Execution-Driven**

**Structural (Permanent Decline Segments):**
1. **Custom Engineering / Retrofit Services** (down 50%): Likely permanent; market shifted to OEM solutions
   - Recommendation: **Exit these service lines** or **divest as separate unit**
2. **Fixed Overhead Burden**: Legacy cost structure cannot be supported at current revenue; requires operational footprint consolidation
   - Recommendation: **Consolidate to 1–2 regional hubs**; accept 10–15% capacity loss

**Execution-Driven (Recoverable):**
1. **Service Delivery Failures** (65% of problem): SLA misses driving churn; fixable in 8–12 weeks
   - Recovery Potential: **+$1.5M revenue** (utilization improvement) + **+$300K EBITDA** (cost avoidance)
2. **Share-of-Wallet Loss in Shared Customers** (key lever): 40–50% of revenue from shared accounts; under-penetrated
   - Recovery Potential: **+$1M revenue** at existing margins = **+$220K EBITDA**
3. **Pricing Discipline & Margin Recovery** (low-hanging fruit): Discount creep; margin compression fixable
   - Recovery Potential: **+$500K–$800K EBITDA** (5–8% margin improvement)
4. **Sales & Account Management** (structural refocus): Move from broad product lines to focused specialization
   - Recovery Potential: **+$500K–$1M revenue** (new customer penetration) + improved retention

---

## PART 6: TURNAROUND PLAN – 12-MONTH CREDIBLE PATH TO PROFITABILITY

### **Strategic Repositioning: From Full-Service Industrial-Services → Focused Maintenance & Reliability Specialist**

---

### **PHASE 1: Diagnostic & Quick-Win Execution (Weeks 1–4)**

**Goal:** Establish credibility; unblock obvious problems; stabilize team

#### **Week 1–2: Deep Diagnostic**
- Complete revenue, margin, utilization, churn analysis (per diagnostic framework above)
- Win/loss interviews (10 lost customers, 5 recent wins)
- SLA audit for top 10 customers
- **Deliverable:** Root-cause diagnostic summary (this document)

#### **Week 2–3: Customer & Org Alignment**
- Meet with top 20 customers (shared + standalone); ask: "What's needed to grow your spend with us?"
- Conduct leadership alignment session with group division heads on shared-customer strategy
- Finalize retention bonus plan for top 20 staff (tie to Q2 & Q4 milestones)
- **Deliverable:** Customer feedback summary; shared-customer account plans; org incentive plan

#### **Week 3–4: Quick-Wins Initiative**
- **SLA Recovery:** Commit to 100% SLA compliance by end of Q2; identify operational fixes (scheduling, staffing)
  - Assign SLA owner; weekly tracking with customers
- **Shared-Customer Initiative:** Launch 5 pilot account plans with other group divisions (joint sales/service meetings)
  - Target: +5% revenue from these accounts by Q2 (= $250K–$500K)
- **Pricing Discipline:** Audit current discounts; implement no-discount->10% policy
  - Training for sales team; tie bonuses to gross profit

#### **Week 4: Executive Alignment & Communication**
- Present diagnostic to board; get alignment on turnaround strategy (vs. exit decision)
- All-hands meeting: communicate turnaround vision, milestones, why it's credible
- **Deliverable:** Board memo + credibility narrative for staff

---

### **PHASE 2: Core Turnaround Execution (Weeks 5–26)**

#### **Workstream 1: Service Delivery Excellence**

**Objective:** Achieve 98%+ SLA compliance; improve utilization from 68% → 78%+

**Tactics:**
1. **Scheduling & Dispatch Optimization** (Week 5–8)
   - Map current dispatch process; identify scheduling gaps (e.g., jobs backfilled last-minute; technicians over-allocated)
   - Implement simple scheduling tool (Excel-based or low-cost software); weekly capacity reviews
   - **Target:** Reduce scheduling variance; improve 1st-time fix rates (reduce rework churn)
   - **Metric:** On-time job start %; first-time fix rate
   - **Owner:** Operations lead

2. **Technician Quality & Training** (Week 5–16)
   - Audit skill gaps (what certifications/training needed?); create fast-track training plan for top technicians
   - Document "best practice" job procedures; standardize across regions
   - Incentivize certification/skill development (bonus for attaining new certifications)
   - **Target:** Improve service quality scores; reduce rework
   - **Metric:** Certification rate; rework %
   - **Owner:** Technical training lead

3. **Customer Feedback Loop** (Week 6–ongoing)
   - Post-job NPS survey (1-question: "Would you recommend?") sent within 24 hours
   - Weekly customer feedback review; root-cause analysis of detractors
   - Escalate promoters to account managers; target for deeper relationships
   - **Target:** Achieve NPS >50 by Q3
   - **Metric:** NPS score; promoter/detractor %; response rate
   - **Owner:** Customer success lead

**Expected Outcome:** 
- Utilization 68% → 75–78% = +$1.5M revenue
- Margin preservation/improvement = +$300K–$500K EBITDA
- Churn stabilization (retain top 5 customers at risk)

---

#### **Workstream 2: Shared-Customer Penetration & Account Growth**

**Objective:** Grow revenue from shared customers by 10% ($1M+); build "group ecosystem" selling model

**Tactics:**
1. **Account Planning with Group Divisions** (Week 5–10)
   - Identify 15–20 high-potential shared customers where other divisions are active but unit is thin
   - Joint meetings (unit + group division reps) with customer; develop joint business plan ("What are customer's biggest pain points? How can group solve?")
   - Identify cross-sell opportunities (e.g., customer buying equipment from division X; unit can provide maintenance + engineering)
   - **Target:** 10 pilot accounts with signed joint plans
   - **Metric:** # of accounts with signed plans; identified opportunities
   - **Owner:** Sales director (new hire or external hire if current incumbent weak)

2. **Account Manager Deployment** (Week 5–12)
   - Assign dedicated account manager per top 10 shared accounts (don't over-assign; 2–3 accounts per AM)
   - Job spec: 3–5 customer conversations/week; quarterly business reviews; proactive solution selling

- **Target:** Labour cost % → 11–12% by Month 6 (from current 13–14%) via utilization recovery

**Owner:** CFO + Sales director
**Budget:** $50K–$75K (job-costing system, training, audit labor)
**Expected Outcome:**
- Gross margin improvement: 22% → 23% by Month 3 = +$205K EBITDA
- Average discount: 12% → 10% = pricing discipline embedded
- Job-margin realization: 90% → 95% = +$150K–$200K annual (scope creep recovery)

---

#### **Workstream 4: Organizational Communication & Talent Stabilization**

**Week 4–5: All-Hands Kickoff & Communication Campaign**
- All-hands meeting (in-person + virtual): Turnaround strategy, why it's credible, role of each team
  - Present diagnostic findings (simplified): "Here's what's broken (service, pricing, focus) and how we fix it"
  - Show 12-month roadmap: milestones, KPIs, how to measure progress
  - Introduce leadership team; reiterate commitment to the plan
  - Q&A: address fears, clarify strategy
- Follow-up: Monthly all-hands (brief updates); weekly divisional huddles (ops, sales, service)
- Internal newsletter: Monthly progress updates; celebrate quick wins

**Week 3–12: Talent Retention & Leadership Stability**
- Execute retention bonus plans (Tier 1): Top 20 staff; 20–50% of salary; paid at Month 6 & 12 milestones
  - Condition: Continued employment; no transfers to other divisions
- Performance management reset: Align individual KPIs to turnaround plan
  - Ops staff: Utilization, SLA compliance, churn, cost management
  - Sales team: Revenue growth (shared-customer focus), gross profit, customer NPS
  - Service team: Utilization, first-time fix rate, customer satisfaction
- Monthly 1:1s: Manager check-ins on turnaround progress + personal development
- **Target:** Voluntary turnover <5% (Months 2–3); top 20 staff stay through Month 6 milestone

**Owner:** HR director + CFO
**Budget:** $500K–$750K (retention bonuses)
**Expected Outcome:**
- Staff retention: Voluntary departures <3% (vs. historical 8–10%)
- Engagement survey: Score improvement by Month 6 (baseline typically low in crisis; target 15+ pt improvement)
- Leadership team stability: No additional departures; clear succession plan in place

---

### **Month 2–3 KPI Targets (End of Quarter 1)**

|---|---|---|---|
| **Service Delivery** | | | |
| SLA Compliance (%) | 82% (est.) | 95%+ | Scheduling, quality fixes take 4–8 weeks; rapid improvement |
| First-Time Fix Rate (%) | 85% | 90%+ | Training + standardization; rework reduction |
| On-Time Job Start (%) | 75% | 90%+ | Scheduling optimization; weekly tracking |
| **Revenue & Margin** | | | |
| Order Book (12-mo visibility) | Declining | Flat / −2% decline | Stabilization; shared-customer pipeline active |
| Gross Margin (%) | 22% | 22–23% | Initial pricing discipline; labor efficiency |
| Revenue (monthly avg) | $1.7M | $1.8M | +5% QoQ (shared-customer quick wins; utilization) |
| **Customer Health** | | | |
| Churn Rate (12-mo) | 12–15% | <12% | SLA recovery + account management reduce attrition |
| Shared-Customer NPS | <30 (est.) | 35–45 | Service improvements; feedback loops active |
| Customer Retention (Tier 1 + 2) | 90% | 95%+ | Account management + SLA recovery |
| **Operational** | | | |
| Billable Utilization (%) | 68% | 70–72% | Scheduling optimization; capacity reallocation |
| Revenue/FTE | $394K | $410K–$420K | Improved utilization without headcount cuts |
| Voluntary Turnover (%) | 8–10% (annual) | <3% (Q1) | Retention bonuses + cred

step_logs.name: Step 1: Financial & Operational Diagnostician
step_logs.system_prompt: You are a financial diagnostician for a struggling industrial-services division. Analyze: three years of consecutive losses despite two restructuring attempts; shrinking order book; departing managers; shared customers with profitable group divisions. Distinguish whether losses are STRUCTURAL (market decline, uncompetitive positioning, flawed business model) or EXECUTION-DRIVEN (cost overruns, operational inefficiency, weak sales, pricing power lost). Examine revenue per customer, gross margins by service line, customer retention/churn, overhead absorption, pricing vs. competition, capacity utilization. Output detailed diagnostic summary with root-cause analysis and structural vs. execution classification.

step_logs.name: Step 2: Segmentation & Strategy Architect
step_logs.system_prompt: You are a strategist designing turnaround and exit options. (A) Segment customers and service lines by profitability, growth potential, and strategic value (especially cross-sell with profitable group divisions). Rank by 12-month profit potential and retention risk. (B) Design a concrete 12-month turnaround plan addressing root causes: revenue initiatives (pricing, cross-sell, target wins), cost restructuring (headcount, overhead, procurement), operational improvements, talent actions. Specify month-by-month milestones with KPIs (revenue targets, margin improvement, order book growth, manager retention %). (C) Design alternative exit pathways (full divestment, partial sale, spin-off, wind-down) with financial scenarios. (D) Define CLEAR DECISION CRITERIA: What specific metrics and thresholds at Month 3, 6, 9 trigger divestment vs. turnaround continuation? (e.g., if order book declines >10% by Month 3 or EBIT margin does not improve 200bps by Month 6, initiate exit). Output profitable segments identified, 12-month roadmap with quarterly targets, exit alternatives, and turnaround-vs-exit decision rules.
